about: Local voice catalog. A menu of starting points, never a fence: any installed voice not listed here may still be cast (as an invented choice with a reason).

kokoro.label: Kokoro-82M (neural)
kokoro.licence: weights Apache-2.0; runtime kokoro-onnx MIT; phonemizer GPL-3.0 and espeak-ng GPL-3.0 are installed separately into the user venv, never shipped in the package
kokoro.source: model files: GitHub release assets of the kokoro-onnx project (tag model-files-v1.1); runtime: PyPI

supports.emphasis: forced primary stress on the word's phonemes
supports.word_timings: yes — per-phoneme durations from the model's duration output, grouped into words

piper.label: Piper (fast neural)
piper.licence: piper-tts 1.8.0 is GPL-3.0-or-later; installed separately into its own user venv and run through its own command line (never vendored, never imported by package code). Each voice carries its own model-card licence (see voices).
piper.licence_note: The last MIT-licensed release (piper-tts 1.2.0) needs piper-phonemize 1.1.0, which publishes no macOS arm64 wheel, so it cannot install on this class of machine.
piper.source: runtime: PyPI piper-tts; voices: the piper-voices model repository, pinned to revision 5041a7a49ae5b3a0f30e6837769eb03fdbb231bd

files.name: en_US-ljspeech-medium.onnx
files.licence: dataset public domain (LJ Speech); voice trained from scratch

files.name: en_GB-cori-medium.onnx
files.licence: dataset public domain (LibriVox recordings); voice trained from scratch

files.name: en_US-norman-medium.onnx
files.licence: dataset public domain (LibriVox recordings); voice trained from scratch

piper.voice_selection_rule: only voices trained from scratch on public-domain recordings were chosen; voices whose dataset or base checkpoint carries a non-commercial or research-only licence were skipped (hfc_female, hfc_male, ryan: CC BY-NC(-SA); semaine: CC BY-NC-SA; lessac: research-licence dataset, and most other voices are fine-tuned from it)

supports.word_timings: no — the command line gives none (the library can, with an extra package, but the package keeps piper at arm's length); use the E2 fallback aligner

say.label: macOS system voice
say.licence: part of macOS (Apple licence); not redistributed

supports.word_timings: no — `say` writes audio only; use the E2 fallback aligner

espeak-ng.label: eSpeak NG (formant, optional)
espeak-ng.licence: GPL-3.0; used only when the user already has it on PATH

voice_attributes_method: warmth, energy and pitch come from MEASURING each voice on one fixed 27-word passage (voices.py profile), not from listening: warmth = 1 - percentile of spectral centroid; energy = mean percentile of pitch spread (clipped at 10 semitones), loudness variation and speaking rate; pitch register from median f0 (<135 Hz low, <=185 mid, else high). clarity = the engine's published training-data grade (Kokoro) or a quality tier (Piper medium, OS voices). best_for follows fixed thresholds on those numbers. Percentiles are relative to the non-novelty voices measured on 2026-10-22.
